name: Neri Oxman
description: Neri Oxman pioneered the discipline she termed Material Ecology, integrating computational design, additive manufacturing, and synthetic biology to produce structures that behave like living organisms, distributing material properties continuously across three-dimensional forms. Her Mediated Matter group at MIT created landmark works including Silk Pavilion — a structure co-fabricated by silkworms guided by robotic trajectories — and Wanderers, 3D-printed wearables hosting photosynthetic microorganisms. Her research introduced multi-material 3D printing techniques that have been commercialized in partnership with Stratasys and widely adopted for biomimetic prosthetics. Oxman was named among TIME's 100 Most Influential People and received the Cooper Hewitt National Design Award. She stepped back from academia in 2019 but her design frameworks continue to influence biomedical device engineering and architectural fabrication.
